newsitem.title: USA: New York City police arrest 32 in weapons raid.
newsitem.headline: New York City police arrest 32 in weapons raid.

text.p: New York City police on Tuesday were investigating the discovery of a weapons cache allegedly belonging to a self-styled radical group who hid the arms in a maze of tunnels and cellars beneath buildings in the city's borough of Brooklyn.
Thirty-two people were arrested in the early morning raid in Brooklyn's Crown Heights neighbourhood after police responded to a report of possible child abuse.
Police said they found more than 40 weapons, including semi-automatic machineguns, shotguns, handguns and rifles, and thousands of rounds of ammunition.
The weapons were found in three houses connected on the ground level after walls were knocked down, and some of the arms were hidden behind a wall and in a ceiling, police said.

The occupants of the houses called themselves the Provisional Party of Communism, and police said they found pamphlets on political organising, particularly among migrant workers, and on telephone soliciting.
The houses were filled with office supplies and equipment, computers and file cabinets, they said.

One woman, who allegedly beat a child with a belt, was charged with endangering the welfare of a child, and four women and one man were charged with weapons possession, police said. The others were expected to be released.
The report of possible child abuse came from a neighbour, police said. Three children were removed from the buildings and placed in custody, they said.

Police said the suspects apparently lived communally in the houses, and neighbours said they lived quietly. The weapons appeared to be for defensive purposes rather than an offensive action, according to officials.
Law enforcement authorities raided the same location in 1984 and recovered gun parts, but no arrests were made.
